title: [finding] A non-skills lane cannot satisfy the governed fork's at-tier review rule for a PR that touches `skills/**` — the tier it requires is reserved away from every lane that can hit it
body:
## Summary

Two standing rules form an **unsatisfiable conjunction** for any PR that lands in a non-skills lane while touching `skills/**`:

| rule | text |
|:--|:--|
| the governed ACCEPT fork | 「① 复核结论照常写在 issue 上;**技能面 PR 的复核席须跑在契约复审档位**。」 |
| the tier ruling (#17285, merged as PR #17294) | the contract-review tier is **reserved** for the skills seat, the spec seat's clause-② review, and the maintainer-summoned director; 「triage and every other seat run the default tier」 |

⇒ A `domain:cli` (or `domain:engine`, `domain:services`, …) seat that reviews a `skills/**`-touching PR **cannot satisfy the first rule without violating the second**. There is no spelling of "run the review at contract-review tier" available to it.

## How it was hit

**PR #17462** (card #17134, `domain:cli`, p1) fixes `os migrate meta --to`'s default. That change makes a prescribed acceptance step in the **published** skill `skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md` false — the skill told authors to run `os migrate meta --from 17` and expect *"Nothing to migrate"*, which the fix turns into "Applied 5 mechanical change(s)". Under the standing rule that a published claim this round turns false must be **repaired, not filed**, the delivery correctly repaired it (+8/-3, ratchet green, well inside every ceiling).

⇒ An ordinary lane card with no `skills/**` ambition acquired a governed surface **as a consequence of being correct**. That is not an edge case to design away — it is what the repair-don't-file rule produces, and it will recur.

The `domain:cli` seat then: took the governed four-piece path, recorded the review on the card, hung `needs-user-decision`, posted the final 维护者速读 on the PR, and requested review from both authorised approver accounts — **and declared in writing that its review was default-tier and therefore NOT the at-tier review rule ① calls for.** ⛔ It did not quietly claim the tier it lacks, and ⛔ it did not skip the rule silently.

## Why this is a finding rather than a note

It is category (b): a **declared rule that cannot be complied with**. The failure is silent by construction — a seat that does not notice the conjunction will simply write "reviewed" and move on, and nothing mechanical reads the reviewer's tier. ⛔ No gate can catch it; the only signal is a seat reading both rules at once and saying so.

⚠️ It also has a plausible **worse** failure mode than the one observed: a seat that *does* notice might route around it by asking the dev to split the `skills/**` hunk into a separate PR — which the governed fork explicitly forbids handling by proportion (「混合 diff ⛔ 不按比例判;要拆让 dev 单独开 PR」 is about *splitting*, not about dodging the review), and which would leave the published skill false for however long the split PR waits.

## Candidate resolutions (⛔ not a ruling — the skills seat decides)

1. **Narrow rule ①** to the skills lane's own PRs, and let the maintainer's review be the gate for a governed surface reached from another lane — which is what the four-piece set already delivers.
2. **Add an explicit carve-out**: a non-skills seat reviewing an incidental `skills/**` hunk reviews at its own tier and must *declare* the tier in the ACCEPT (which is what happened here, ad hoc).
3. **Route the review**: the reviewing seat hands the `skills/**` hunk to the skills seat for an at-tier review before the four-piece set fires.

⚠️ Option 3 is the only one that preserves rule ① literally, and it is also the only one that adds a cross-seat hop to every incidental one-line skill repair. That trade is the decision.

## Not duplicates (checked, including closed)

Searched the tier/contract-review family; the closest neighbours are **#17285** (the ruling that creates one half of the conjunction — closed), **#16905** (dropped the tier mandate for clause-② *implementation*, a different axis — closed), **#16914** (stale clause-② prose in `dispatch-gates` — open, different subject), and **#13587** (a one-off "review and land the `skills/**` half authored across a lane line" — closed, an instance rather than the rule gap). ⛔ None states this conjunction.

Filed by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024, session `session_01DapQyvYrFb1MxSYe7BL2nt`) out of PR #17462's governed-path review. ⛔ Not graded, no `domain:*`, no priority, no assignee — that is triage's. ⚠️ Suggested lane: this is protocol text ⇒ `domain:skills`.
